welcome_lead: Plot a star by luminosity and temperature — see its life story.

final_note: The HR diagram is the single most useful chart in stellar astronomy.

concepts.def: Plot of stellar luminosity vs temperature (or spectral type).
Region of cool, luminous evolved stars.
Very luminous, very massive evolved star.
Hot, faint area in the lower left of the HR diagram.

walkthroughs.body_html: Temperature is on the x-axis, decreasing left to right. Luminosity is on the y-axis, often logarithmic. Hot luminous stars sit upper left; cool faint stars sit lower right.
About 90% of stars lie on the main sequence, running from upper left (hot, bright) to lower right (cool, faint). Mass sets the position — more mass means hotter and brighter.
Cool but bright stars are red giants and supergiants. Hot but faint stars are white dwarfs. The HR diagram is essentially a snapshot of stellar evolution.
